content:
alex: heads-up — canary #3 (mixed-precision runtime change) is showing a p95 token latency spike for short seqs, noticed in prod-like load.
priya: how big a spike? numbers please.
alex: p50 about the same (18ms -> 20ms), p95 jumped from ~55ms to ~130ms on the canary hosts for seq_len <= 24, batching ~4-8.
sam: interesting. does the trace point at scheduling/batching or the kernel itself?
alex: captured a perf trace (nvtx + pprof). root cause looks like kernel-selection + padding blowup: the selector picks an FP8 tile kernel that requires 32-aligned tiles, so short sequences get padded a lot and then we fall back to a slower kernel path, causing extra memcopies and KV cache churn.
priya: can you paste the selector config we used in the canary?
alex: sure — snippet:
```
# kernel_selector.conf
rules:
  - prefer: fp8_kernel
    min_tokens: 64
  - fallback: int8_kernel
    max_padding_ratio: 0.2
```
priya: that prefactor (min_tokens: 64) seems optimistic for short-chat workloads. padding_ratio check maybe not doing what we expect with continuous batching.
sam: +1. also saw KV cache append path misalign slabs when sequences are small and batching mixes seqs; extra memcpy to realign KV pages shows up in the trace.
taylor: do we have a microbench harness that reproduces the short-seq + mixed-quant path deterministically?
alex: I ran a microbench that replays shapes: [(4,8),(6,12),(2,20)] under continuous-batcher and recorded kernel choices. Results: 42% calls went FP8-tile (with heavy padding), 18% fallback to slow path, and p95 matched the canary.
priya: could we change selector to prefer int8 for seq_len < 32 or when padding_ratio > 0.15? Simple heuristic to reduce waste.
sam: Another option: add a fast-path kernel for small shapes (quantized 4-bit fused path) that avoids tile-alignment padding. But that's more engineering time.
alex: quick experiment — changed rule in memory on 3 hosts: prefer int8 if seq_len <= 24. Microbench after change: p95 dropped from 130ms -> 68ms, throughput +11% on those hosts.
priya: nice. any regression for longer sequences?
alex: none observed for seq>128; FP8 still selected there. We should check quality impact for int8 on those short contexts.
taylor: can we run a correctness sweep (generation/llm-evals) for the int8-on-short-seq change? Mark as canary-only toggle.
sam: also want to fix the KV slab alignment bug — short sequences + mixed batch ordering trigger suboptimal slab copies. I'll open a small PR to change KV append to try a borrow/append instead of realignment when free space exists.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary #3 rolled out to 5 hosts at 1768899950, rollback allowed until 1768901200.
priya: plan: 1) roll the selector heuristic change as a canary config (prefer int8 if seq_len < 32 or padding_ratio > 0.15), 2) run full eval sweep for quality, 3) land KV-append alignment fix. If canary p95 < 80ms and eval delta < 0.5% for our smoke prompts, promote.
alex: I'll draft the selector config PR + benchmark results (include nvprof traces). Sam will own KV change.
taylor: add unit tests for kernel selector decision matrix and an integration microbench in CI. also add telemetry for padding_ratio and chosen_kernel to help future debugging.
priya: sounds good. create the PRs and ping #eng-runtime when ready. thanks :thumbsup:
alex: uploaded traces to /artifacts/canary-3/1768899999/ and linked them in the PR.
sam: opened github.com/redwood/inference/pull/892 with KV append fix; contains perf before/after.
priya: we'll hold on wide rollout until both selector + KV fixes land and canary shows stable p95 < 80ms.
